manufacturing.steps_title: From the drawing to the truck

steps.title: Shop drawings
steps.description: We draw every opening — wall heights, pan size, drain position, niche and accessory locations — and hold production until you sign off.

steps.title: Fabrication
steps.description: Panels and pans are cast and cut to the approved dimensions.

steps.title: Quality hold
steps.description: Colour, thickness and edge are checked against the approved finish sample before anything is packed.

steps.title: Crating
steps.description: Panels are foam-separated, banded and crated in wood. Every crate is labelled with the project, the floor and the unit it belongs to.

steps.title: Staged or shipped
steps.description: The order ships straight to the jobsite, or we hold it in our warehouse under the storage agreement until your schedule calls it in.

shipping.title: The truck arrives when your floor is ready for it
shipping.description: Material moves on a flatbed straight from our plant to your site. There is no distributor in the middle, which is why the crate you open is the crate we packed. Everything below is what your site superintendent needs to know before the driver pulls up.

phases.title: Delivery window
phases.description: We confirm the delivery date two weeks out and call the site the day before. Tell us the access constraints — dock height, street permits, crane windows — when you place the order, not when the truck is outside.

phases.title: How it arrives
phases.description: Flatbed truck, wooden crates and banded pallets. The driver is not responsible for unloading: the site supplies the equipment and the crew.

phases.title: Partial and phased releases
phases.description: Multi-tower and phased jobs can be released floor by floor or wing by wing so you are not storing material you will not hang for two months.

phases.title: Container shipments
phases.description: For projects outside the continental US we crate for container loading and provide the packing list and dimensions your freight forwarder needs.

equipment.title: What you need on site to unload
equipment.description: Have this staged before the truck is scheduled. A truck that cannot be unloaded within the free time on the bill of lading accrues detention against the project.
rows: Forklift with 48" forks and a pallet jack
equipment.note: A shower pan weighs roughly 200 lb. Nothing on the truck is a two-hand carry.

receiving.title: Receiving and inspection
receiving.description: Five minutes at the tailgate is the difference between a replacement panel and an argument with a freight carrier.
items: Count the crates against the bill of lading before you sign anything.
Walk the load while it is still on the truck and photograph every crushed corner, tear or shifted band.
Write the damage on the delivery receipt. A clean signature closes the carrier's liability.
Open and inspect the panels within 48 hours of delivery.
Keep the crate labels — the project and unit number on them is how we identify a replacement.

storage.title: Storage on site
storage.description: Material is finished goods from the moment it leaves our plant. Store it like it is.
items: Indoors, dry, out of direct sun and away from any heat source.
Crates flat and off the slab on dunnage; panels stored on edge, never face down.
Do not stack more than two panel crates high.
Warehouse storage past 30 days from the ready-to-ship date falls under our storage agreement.

claims.title: Damage and claims
claims.description: Report it fast and we replace it fast.
items: Visible damage: note it on the delivery receipt at the tailgate and send photos the same day.
Concealed damage: report within five business days of delivery.
Send the crate label, the bill of lading number and photos of the crate and the panel.
We confirm within two business days and put approved replacements into expedited fabrication.

shipping.returns_note: Every panel and pan is cut for one specific opening, so material cannot be returned for credit. Order the overage you want with the original release, not after.

warranty.title: One supplier for the wall and the pan — so one warranty
warranty.description: Because we fabricate everything in one facility, there is no gap between claims to argue about. Terms below are our standard commercial coverage; project-specific terms follow your contract documents.

coverage.title: Wall panels & shower pans
coverage.description: Manufacturing defects, delamination and cracking not caused by impact or substrate movement.

coverage.title: Accessories & trim
coverage.description: Niches, soap dishes, shelves, footrests and trim strips against manufacturing defect.

included.title: Included
items: Manufacturing defects in material or finish
Delamination or separation under normal use
Cracking not caused by impact or building movement
Colour variation outside our published tolerance
Replacement material fabricated to the original drawing

excluded.title: Not included
items: Impact damage, dropped tools and site abuse
Abrasive pads, scouring powders and bleach-based cleaners
Adhesives, sealants or fasteners we did not specify
Field modifications made after delivery
Movement, settlement or failure of the substrate behind the panel

claim.title: Making a claim
steps: Email us the project name, the unit or room number and photographs of the condition.
We respond within two business days with an assessment or a site visit.
Approved claims go into expedited fabrication and ship to the site.

care.title: Care & maintenance
care.description: Non-porous surfaces do not need sealing, ever. They do need the right cleaner.
items: Daily: a standard non-abrasive shower cleaner, then rinse completely.
Weekly: warm water and a soft cloth on the joints and the pan.
Quarterly: a deep clean per the care sheet restores gloss on high-traffic units.
Never: abrasive pads, scouring powder, bleach-based scrubs or solvent cleaners.

faq.title: The questions we answer most
faq.description: If yours is not here, a specialist will answer it in one business day.

items.q: How is this different from tile?
items.a: It is a panel system, not individual tiles and grout. You get the look of a tiled wall as one continuous surface, with no grout lines to seal, scrub or replace, and a project measured in days rather than weeks.

items.q: How is it different from acrylic or fiberglass?
items.a: Acrylic and fiberglass units are thin shells. Our panels and pans are solid surface all the way through, so they take commercial traffic, hold a repair and do not flex underfoot.

items.q: Is it really waterproof without a membrane?
items.a: Yes. The surface is non-porous and the joints are sealed with 100% silicone, so water never reaches the substrate.

items.q: Does it stain or grow mildew?
items.a: The surface is non-porous, so it does not absorb. Mildew has nothing to root into and common bathroom stains wipe off. There is no grout to discolour.

items.q: Can I get a colour that is not one of the five standard finishes?
items.a: Yes. The five standard finishes cover every pattern and ship on the standard lead time. Custom colours are available on request and are quoted per project.
We work project by project rather than by the piece. Small residential jobs are welcome — tell us the rough openings and we will tell you honestly whether we are the right fit.

items.q: What is the standard lead time?
items.a: Four to six weeks from approved shop drawings to the truck, depending on the size of the release. Everything is made to order, so the clock starts at approval, not at the purchase order.

items.q: How do I get a sample?
items.a: Request one from any product page or from the contact form. We send physical finish chips so you are approving the colour in the room's own light, not on a screen.
No. Every wall pattern in the catalog is the same price per square foot. What changes by pattern is the available mould size, which we work out on the shop drawing.

items.q: Can you make a size that is not in the catalog?
items.a: Yes — most pans and surrounds are custom sizes already. Send the rough opening and the drain position and we will draw it.
Yes. Say it is a model room when you request the quote so we release it ahead of the main run and match the finish for the production units later.

items.q: Can we return extra material for credit?
items.a: No. Everything is cut for one specific opening and is not stocked, so it cannot be resold.
On a flatbed truck straight from our plant, in wooden crates and on banded pallets, labelled by floor and unit. Nothing is cross-docked.

items.q: What equipment do we need to unload?
items.a: A forklift with 72-inch forks for wall panel crates, and a forklift with 48-inch forks plus a pallet jack for shower pans. The driver does not unload.

items.q: What if a crate arrives damaged?
items.a: Note it on the delivery receipt before you sign, photograph it on the truck and send us the photos with the crate label and bill of lading number. Concealed damage has a five-business-day window.

items.q: Can you hold our order until the site is ready?
items.a: Yes. We warehouse finished orders and release them floor by floor. Storage past 30 days from the ready-to-ship date falls under the storage agreement.

items.q: Do you ship outside the continental US?
items.a: Yes, crated for container loading. We provide the packing list, crate dimensions and weights your freight forwarder.
